reporting_note: Aramco discloses disruption at the level of financial materiality; the energy ministry issues statements after attacks. There is no event register, so the coverage of this record cannot be computed.

geography.note: 13 regions (ISO SA-01 to SA-14; there is no SA-13). Official electricity statistics are reported by four operating areas, not these regions.

rulings.note: Includes the Saudi share of the former Saudi-Kuwaiti Neutral Zone.

sectors.reason: Denominator ready: Aramco's annual report lists all nine in-Kingdom refineries (gross basis). Four are joint ventures, so numerator and denominator must come from the same gross rows. Not scored. The recovery and decay model behind the Monitored-Area ESDI was calibrated on repeated strikes with almost no restart reporting, and no model for this country's events has been approved (GLOBAL_METHODOLOGY.md §2 and §8.3).
National grid-connected capacity is published quarterly, but no plant list.
National aggregates only; the event-burden measure does not fit.
The ESDI's refining-base proxy breaks for a crude exporter: one export terminal would exceed 100% of it.
Processing capacities are EIA estimates; there is no domestic LNG.
Not applicable: Saudi Arabia has no coal production or coal power (EIA reports zero). The sector does not exist here, which is different from unknown.

research_gaps: Non-conflict incidents remain thin: the July 2024 Sharurah outage is reported in residents (over 100,000), not customers, and is held rather than converted.
The record is dominated by conflict episodes (March 2022, and 2026). That reflects how Saudi incidents are reported, not the absence of other disruption.
